plan.disposition: BUG path at medium: the mini-plan is the F-debug four-phase investigation recorded in the iterate spec; no separate plan artifact was produced, so there was no plan document to review. Design decisions were instead reviewed as code by the spec/code/doubt cascade.

code.raw_excerpt:
Stage-2 code-quality review (shipwright-build:code-reviewer, opus) — VERDICT: FAIL
(1 blocking, 6 should-fix, 6 nits). Reviewed shared/scripts/lib/atomic_write.py,
its tests, file_lock.py, run_config_store.py, phase_task_lifecycle.py,
step_planning.py and the changelog hunk.

Confirmed sound: the retry loop's deadline arithmetic, temp-file cleanup on every
path including KeyboardInterrupt, no swallowed failure mode, no half-published
destination. Explicit deadlock analysis across every lock that can be held across
durable_atomic_write: run_config_lock, _PhaseTasksLock and file_lock all target a
.lock SIDECAR, never the destination, so no self-deadlock is possible; worst case
is bounded amplification.

BLOCKING 1 — the changelog fix sterilised literals but the message interpolates
untrusted data ({changelog_path}, {version}); a non-ASCII project path reproduces
the identical failure, and the new test used an ASCII tmp_path so its green
certified the fixture, not the code. FIXED: moved to a source-level fix (the CLI
pins stdout+stderr to utf-8) and the test now uses a non-ASCII project directory.
Verified against the pre-fix module: 0xfc at position 61.

2 — exception filter may miss ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION (33) / ERROR_USER_MAPPED_FILE
(1224). DECLINED ON EVIDENCE: probed on Windows 11 — a memory-mapped holder and a
byte-range lock both surface as PermissionError winerror 5. Premise did not
reproduce. The related point that winerror 5 is ALSO the generic access-denied
code was CONFIRMED by probe (read-only destination and directory destination both
give 5) and is now stated honestly in the code and pinned by a test.

3 — the Windows branch has no CI coverage (ci.yml is ubuntu-only). DECLINED here:
adding a workflow leg trips touches_ci_supplychain and its acknowledgement gate;
that is its own decision, not a rider on a bug fix. Injected-failure tests give
Linux CI real coverage of the retry logic.

4 — the cleanup os.unlink can itself hit a sharing violation, leaving .tmp debris,
so AC3 overclaimed. ACCEPTED: AC3 reworded to best-effort-on-Windows with the
reason stated.

5 — two unrelated fixes in one commit harms bisectability. DECLINED: the F11
verifier checks a single F6 commit. Kept as separate self-contained hunks and
named separately in the commit body.

6 — the exhaustion test could spin forever (no pytest-timeout configured).
ACCEPTED: added an elapsed-time bound.

7 — the primitive-level fix leaves the in-repo unlocked reader
(_read_standalone_flag) untouched and the docstring implied closure. ACCEPTED:
docstring now states the retry is a mitigation for holders we do not control and
that our own unlocked reader remains a separately-recorded trade-off.

Nits: inert `# noqa: SIM115` for a rule this repo does not enable (ACCEPTED,
removed); timer not joined / reader not closed in finally (ACCEPTED, try/finally +
cancel); REPLACE_RETRY_BUDGET_SECONDS missing from __all__ (ACCEPTED, added);
helper name over-narrow (ACCEPTED, renamed to _replace_retrying_sharing_violations);
docstring phrasing mirror (ACCEPTED); AC6 evidence and changelog drop land at
F4/F5 (ACCEPTED, done).

Note: this reviewer explicitly judged the os.name monkeypatch "not a finding".
That assessment was wrong — the external reviewer caught it and a live probe
confirmed it would have been red on Linux CI. Recorded because it is the clearest
evidence in this run that the reviewers are not substitutable for one another.

doubt.raw_excerpt:
Stage-3 adversarial doubt review (shipwright-build:doubt-reviewer, opus) —
8 doubts: 3 high, 1 medium-high, 2 medium, 2 low. Advisory-must-address.

Survived the attack (reviewer tried to break these and failed): the mechanism is
real, not hypothetical (_read_standalone_flag genuinely reads the run config
outside run_config_lock on every update_step); the retry loop is structurally
correct with a real clamp; _is_windows() is the right fix and the pre-existing
tests were correctly migrated to it; closing the card is reversible because
suite_race_triage dedups against OPEN items only; test_runconfig_concurrency
remains meaningful for the stale-copy-clobber class it exists to catch.

D1 high — winerror 5 is BOTH the sharing-violation symptom and the canonical
genuine-denial code, so a read-only destination or deny-ACL is retried for the
whole budget and the comment claimed a discrimination the code lacks; the 1337
test pinned nothing real. ACCEPTED, PROBED (attrib +R and a directory destination
both return winerror 5). Comment rewritten honestly; the 1337 test relabelled as
a synthetic shape-check; a new test records that a genuine denial IS retried.

D2 high — a SUCCESSFUL retry is silent, so the module swallows the one signal
that would show the unlocked-reader discipline degrading. ACCEPTED AS A LIMIT,
DECLINED AS BUILT-HERE: wiring telemetry out of a primitive with 30 call sites is
a design decision with no consumer today (YAGNI). Now named explicitly in the
module docstring so it is visible rather than implied.

D3 high — the statistics do not support the claim. P(0 failures in 72 | rate
unchanged) = (47/48)^72 = 0.22; rule of three gives a 95% upper bound of 4.2%,
above the pre-fix point estimate. The ORIGINAL failure was never reproduced, its
traceback never captured, and it came from a different worktree at a different
commit — yet the plan presented a traceback under "Phase 1 — Read Error" as if it
were the original observation. FULLY ACCEPTED. The plan now labels the
traceback's provenance, states that the deterministic repro (100% -> 0%) is the
load-bearing evidence and the rate data is corroboration only, and carries a
"What is NOT established" section covering all three points.

D4 medium-high — the retry also widens the window in which an UNLOCKED writer can
publish a STALE snapshot over a newer one; config_io.save_run_config documents
that the lock is held by callers, not the writer, so such writers exist.
ACCEPTED AND VERIFIED against the source. Budget cut 2.0s -> 0.5s (still ~500x a
config read) with the reasoning recorded at the constant.

D5 medium — the changelog fix was literal-only and structurally could not catch
an interpolated non-ASCII path. ACCEPTED; same finding as the code-reviewer's
blocking item. Fixed at the source; test now uses a non-ASCII project directory.

D6 medium — inter-unit pollution was excluded only for the 12-copy configuration,
not for the 18-unit run the card describes, and real pollution exists in the tree.
ACCEPTED: filed as trg-c6e75011 and stated in the plan's "What is NOT established".

D7 low — the budget was chosen against a human, not against the enclosing
timeouts. ACCEPTED implicitly by the cut to 0.5s.

D8 low — claims the parent gets IndexError rather than stderr=None. DISPROVED BY
DIRECT OBSERVATION: `result.stderr is None` is True on Python 3.12.13, and the
original pytest failure was `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not
iterable`. The recorded mechanism stands.

findings.finding: The tests simulate Windows by assigning `aw.os.name = "nt"`, but `aw.os` is the process-global stdlib `os` module. On POSIX, this also changes what `pathlib.Path()` selects. `durable_atomic_write()` immediately executes `Path(path)`, which then attempts to construct a `WindowsPath` on a POSIX host and raises `NotImplementedError` before reaching the retry logic. Thus the new supposedly cross-platform injected-failure tests fail in POSIX CI rather than testing AC1/AC2.
findings.suggestion: Do not monkeypatch global `os.name`. Introduce a narrowly mockable platform predicate in `atomic_write` (for example, `_is_windows()`), or test the helper with string paths while separately testing temp cleanup without changing the platform identity.

findings.finding: The retry sleep is not bounded by the remaining retry budget. If the loop observes time just before `deadline`, it can sleep for up to `_RETRY_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS` beyond the deadline and then successfully replace a destination released after the configured budget. This violates the documented/accepted bounded retry behavior: a destination held past the budget may succeed rather than raising, and failures may return later than the budget.
findings.suggestion: Compute remaining time before sleeping and sleep only `min(delay, max(0, deadline - time.monotonic()))`; if no time remains, re-raise before sleeping or attempting another replace.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The implementation approach is appropriate, but the new platform-simulation tests break POSIX CI and the retry window is not actually bounded to its configured budget.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

[openai] - Category: test
- Severity: high
- File: shared/tests/test_atomic_write.py:198, 223, 241
- Finding: The tests simulate Windows by assigning `aw.os.name = "nt"`, but `aw.os` is the process-global stdlib `os` module. On POSIX, this also changes what `pathlib.Path()` selects. `durable_atomic_write()` immediately executes `Path(path)`, which then attempts to construct a `WindowsPath` on a POSIX host and raises `NotImplementedError` before reaching the retry logic. Thus the new supposedly cross-platform injected-failure tests fail in POSIX CI rather than testing AC1/AC2.
- Suggestion: Do not monkeypatch global `os.name`. Introduce a narrowly mockable platform predicate in `atomic_write` (for example, `_is_windows()`), or test the helper with string paths while separately testing temp cleanup without changing the platform identity.

- Category: bug
- Severity: medium
- File: shared/scripts/lib/atomic_write.py:108-109
- Finding: The retry sleep is not bounded by the remaining retry budget. If the loop observes time just before `deadline`, it can sleep for up to `_RETRY_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS` beyond the deadline and then successfully replace a destination released after the configured budget. This violates the documented/accepted bounded retry behavior: a destination held past the budget may succeed rather than raising, and failures may return later than the budget.
- Suggestion: Compute remaining time before sleeping and sleep only `min(delay, max(0, deadline - time.monotonic()))`; if no time remains, re-raise before sleeping or attempting another replace.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The implementation approach is appropriate, but the new platform-simulation tests break POSIX CI and the retry window is not actually bounded to its configured budget.
